current_difficulty_reason: Taking a convex hull can change BV graph traces and can merge several admissible free-boundary regions, so ordinary convexity and lower semicontinuity do not show that the relaxed energy decreases. The authors derive a graph-current slice estimate for the new trace costs and apply countably many gap-filling operations with controlled area loss, then run a finite merging procedure and rebuild the prescribed endpoint curves. Those new constructive estimates close the nonclosed admissible class while preserving its boundary data, beyond merely applying standard BV compactness.
